newsitem.title: USA: Insured damage from Fran heavy in 7 U.S. states.
newsitem.headline: Insured damage from Fran heavy in 7 U.S. states.

text.p: Seven U.S. states suffered serious insured property damage from Hurricane Fran, according to an insurance industry group.

The states facing the most significant damage included North Carolina, South Carolina, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania and Ohio, said Gary Kerney, assistant vice president for Property Claim Services, an industry- supported group that tracks losses.
PCS expects to have an official estimate of the insured property damage from Hurricane Fran at the end of the week, Kerney said.

Insured damage was unofficially estimated at $625 million on Friday by the Insurance Information Institute. Applied Insurance Research in Boston prepared the preliminary estimate using a computer software program.
However, losses could increase as the industry assesses damage from inland areas and commercial properties.

Damage was heavy not just in sparsely-populated coastal areas, but in some larger cities further inland as well, said Bernhard Schroeder, global property claims manager for insurance broker Johnson & Higgins.
Schroeder said commercial insured damage appeared heavy in Raleigh and Wilmington, N.C. as well as in Richmond, Va.
Insurers can expect to see claims from commercial clients for not just property damage but for business interruption losses as well, he said.
"There are a number of retail clients, manufacturing clients that do have facilities that are down," he said.
"Some are significant due to physical damage where a company's location is just a total loss. We also have a number of clients that are being impacted by a loss of power," he said.
Losses from the interruption of business, he said, were difficult to estimate because it was unclear how long it may take before the business resumes normal operation.
"Our clients don't really know the extent of their losses, he said. "They are having difficulty at this point getting that all identified for themselves," he said.
Even so, he said, the damage from Hurricane Fran appears to be lighter than the damage caused by Hurricane Hugo in 1989.
"It was not as severe as Hugo," he said.
